A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable versions of the same EgoIntention/RoG study. v1's supplementary Sections A-B were inspected. The supplied v2 ends with references and omits that supplementary material despite retaining appendix references; this is an observable document difference.

before.justification: v1 reports original grounding benchmarks, fine-tuning experiments, training-data ablations, annotation-validation results, and supplementary qualitative comparisons.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and adds inter-annotator validation, error analysis, and uncommon-intention training and transfer results.

M1.justification: Sections 4.2-4.3 retain the same procedure: infer an object category using the <reason> token, then ground it using <ref>, with LoRA fine-tuning on hybrid grounding data. RAM++ supports a new analysis, not a new RoG component.

E1.justification: v2 actually evaluates zero-shot transfer on RIO's uncommon-intention set in Table 7; v1 only discusses RIO as related work. EgoIntention, RefCOCO/+/g, and the generated RefCOCOIntention training data remain. This adds a limited external evaluation domain.

E2.justification: The evaluated comparators remain both GPT-4/GroundingDINO pipeline orders, CogVLM-grounding, Groma, MiniGPT-v2, and Qwen-VL, alongside zero-shot, Naive SFT, and RoG variants. The new analyses reuse these variants. RAM++ is an error-assessment tool, not an additional competing grounding method.

E3.justification: v2 adds protocols for a 500-sample inter-annotator study, RAM++-assisted error classification, and inclusion/exclusion of uncommon training data followed by EgoIntention and RIO testing. Existing splits, model sizes, and precision thresholds remain. The newly explicit maximum-IoU rule does not establish whether earlier experiments used different scoring or were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds annotation-reliability validation, separates hallucination from language- and vision-misleading errors in Section 5.6.3, and tests uncommon-training-data contributions and transfer in Section 5.6.4. These substantially extend diagnostic evidence. Conversely, v1's supplementary vocabulary visualizations and four qualitative Naive-versus-RoG grounding examples are absent.

E5.justification: Section 3.2 adds inter-annotator reliability estimation on 500 verified samples, reporting 98.6% agreement for context intentions and 91.2% for uncommon intentions. v1 reported only GPT-human validation agreement/correlation. Neither version reports benchmark uncertainty across seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Core EgoIntention scores are extensively revised: Table 4 changes MiniGPT-v2 RoG overall P@0.5 from 42.64 to 47.3 and Qwen-VL RoG from 34.91 to 33.6. New Tables 6-7 report error rates and uncommon-training effects, including RoG RIO scores of 23.8 without versus 26.0 with uncommon training. These are revised and added results, not established same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Both versions retain the same image-query-to-bounding-box task definition and contain no theoretical propositions or proofs. The maximum-IoU scoring explanation and new empirical error categories do not introduce a theoretical contribution.

C1.justification: The dataset, failure-diagnosis, and model-agnostic RoG contributions retain their scope. However, the introduction strengthens the quantified effectiveness claim: MiniGPT-v2's stated advantage over Naive SFT rises from 3.5 to 3.9 P@0.5 points, and over GPT-4 plus GroundingDINO from 7.5 to 12.2.

C2.justification: v2 adds an argument that annotation agreement and retained RefCOCO performance support dataset quality, and introduces a more explicit failure taxonomy. Its lower-error interpretation needs qualification: Table 6 shows context language-misleading errors of 2.1% for RoG versus 1.4% for Naive SFT, so improvement is not uniform.

D1.justification: v2 omits v1's detailed affordance list, in-context examples, full generation prompts, and MTurk interfaces in supplementary Tables A-C and Figures B/D. It adds explicit second-annotator verification, PACO query-category sourcing, and maximum-IoU scoring documentation. v1 promises future data/code release; v2 supplies a repository link stating code/model availability.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations on egocentric assistance, affordance learning, visual intention grounding, and RAM++, while removing the few-shot-learning and functional-correspondence references associated with v1's supplement. It also emphasizes RIO's lack of uncommon-intention training examples. The principal positioning against existing grounding datasets and models remains.

P1.justification: Rewriting concentrates on annotation validation, hybrid-baseline descriptions, evaluation metrics, and ablation explanations. v2 adds two analysis subsections and acknowledgements and omits supplementary Sections A-B. Most main-text prose and the ordering of Sections 1-6 are preserved.

P2.justification: Figures 1-4 are restyled, with Figure 4 compressed and relocated. v1 Tables 5-6 are merged into v2 Table 5, which adds an average column; new Tables 6-7 display error and uncommon-training analyses. Supplementary Figures A-D and Tables A-C disappear. These substantially revise the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through annotation-agreement validation, error analysis, and RIO transfer tests, and supplies a code/model access pointer. However, the supplied PDF loses v1's detailed prompts, annotation interfaces, and qualitative comparisons while retaining dangling appendix references. The new error interpretation also needs qualification, and higher revised scores cannot establish same-setting gains. These substantive benefits and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
